question.title: Question 46
question.scenario: You are preparing for the Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate certification exam.

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Tokenization is the process of splitting text into smaller units called tokens, which are the fundamental building blocks that language models process and generate.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Tokenization breaks text into discrete units (tokens) that language models can process. Tokens can be whole words, subwords, or individual characters depending on the tokenizer. For example, "unhappiness" might become ["un", "happiness"] or ["un", "happi", "ness"]. Encryption transforms data for security. Caching stores computed results. Compression reduces data size. Tokenization is fundamental because it determines how text is represented numerically, affects context window utilization, and directly impacts billing since Azure OpenAI charges per token.

ul.li: GPT models use Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) via the tiktoken library; a rough approximation is that one token equals about 4 characters or 0.75 words in English.
Non-English languages and code often tokenize less efficiently, using more tokens per word; this affects both cost and context window utilization for multilingual applications.
The tokenizer determines the model's vocabulary size and directly affects what the model can and cannot represent; different model families may use different tokenizers.
For AI-102, use the tiktoken library or Azure OpenAI tokenizer tool to estimate token counts before sending requests, ensuring prompts stay within context limits and cost budgets.
